25:##### Description
27:A task's header shows the compiled markdown that was actually sent to the harness, rendered as markdown, once it has compiled, along with the name of the hidden anchor it was compiled from.
29:#### Status
31:##### Description
33:A task's status is a coloured label that spells it out: "Building" in blue, "Compiling" in cyan, "Running" in yellow, "Done" in green, "Failed" in red, "Cancelled" in orange, and "Not recorded" in grey for a task from the history with no record of its run. The labels are readable in both light and dark mode.
35:##### Elapsed
37:Beside its status label, a task shows how long it has been under way, from when it was sent, building and compiling included, in small muted tabular figures: minutes and seconds, "0:42" or "12:05", with hours ahead of them once it reaches an hour, "1:02:33". While the task is building, compiling, or running, it counts up every second, so a task that seems stuck can be told from one that has only just started. Once the task is over, however it ended, it stops and stays at how long the task took. It shows wherever the status label does, the latest task's header and the heading of each previous task, including a task running in the other lane. A task from the history whose record holds no start and end shows none.
39:#### Output Table
41:##### Description
43:A task's output is a [TaskTableScope](../../../ui/components/task-table/index.md#task-table-scope), whose rows are what the harness did for the task. While the task is under way, its table ends in the waiting row for whatever the harness does next. Tasks never collapse their steps, since their whole chain is of interest.
45:#### Links
47:##### Description
49:Links in the compiled prompt and in reply text are clickable. A link to a file opens it, as the [OpenFileScope](../../open-file/index.md#open-file-scope) says, and a web link opens in the browser. The file path on a Read, Edit, Write, or MultiEdit row is shown as a link and opens that file the same way.
51:#### Backgrounds
53:##### Description
55:The header for the latest task is coloured like the tab the task was sent from, the colour of its mode, of the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope), as the [ChatInputScope](../chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) body shows for that tab. A task from the history that doesn't say which tab it was sent from keeps the tab bar's colour. The queue along the bottom and the previous tasks row along the top both have the same background colour as the tab bar.
56:Each task in the previous tasks list hints at the mode it was sent in: its heading's background is a faint tint of that mode's colour, of the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope), red for Code, purple for Chain, blue for Spec, green for Ask, and grey for Freeform, far fainter than the latest task's header, so the list reads as a column of the list's own background with each task only touched by its colour. A task whose mode isn't known, as one from the history that doesn't say, keeps the list's background untinted. Its status label, prompt, checkbox, and buttons stay readable over the tint, in light and dark mode, and its hover and open states still show over it. An open task's prompt and output beneath its heading are not tinted.
58:#### Referenced Spec
60:##### Description
62:While a task is running, a [RightSidebarScope](../../../ui/components/right-sidebar/index.md#right-sidebar-scope) slides out from the message list's right edge, listing the spec files the task references, and slides back once the run is over.
64:#### Scrolling
66:##### Description
68:The latest task's table scrolls with its lock to the bottom off to start with, until switched on. Each open project keeps how far its latest task's table was scrolled and whether it was locked, and the rest of its message list as it was left, as the [OpenProjectsScope](../../open-projects/index.md#open-projects-scope) says, so switching back to it shows the list just as it was.
69:However long the list of previous tasks grows, drawing it costs no more than drawing the tasks in view, so scrolling, animations, and new output stay smooth.
71:##### Scrolling Past
73:Scrolling carries on past either end of the latest task and the previous tasks, from one to the other, through an elastic stretch at that end. A scroll that reaches an end doesn't stop dead there: the same scroll keeps going, with no pause needed, into the stretch, which resists it, and it crosses over only once it has pushed far enough into the stretch to get past a barrier at its far side. The only scroll that stops at an end is a fling's momentum still running when it gets there, and a scroll that has already crossed over is spent (below).
74:How the view came to be at its end makes no difference. A scroll begun with the view already resting there, scrolled there some time before, opened there by clicking the previous tasks row, or left there when a slide settled, pulls into the stretch from its very first step, exactly as one that scrolls the view there and carries on; it never has to move the view first, and nothing it does is swallowed by the view before the stretch takes it.
75:The barrier is a distance to scroll past. The distance a scroll goes past the end builds up, and it crosses over the moment that reaches 768 pixels, about twelve or thirteen notches of a mouse wheel or a firm swipe on a trackpad, however quickly or slowly it gets there, so the end is felt as a real resistance before the view gives way. The scroll that brings the view to its end counts too: whatever of it goes past the end starts the build-up, rather than being lost. Scrolling back the other way takes the build-up down again, and scrolls the view once it is gone.
76:The build-up never drains while the scroll goes on. A scroll goes on for as long as the wheel or trackpad keeps scrolling, with less than 200 milliseconds between one step and the next, as between the notches of a wheel spun steadily, however slowly; each step adds all of itself to the build-up, so a steady scroll of any speed reaches the barrier and crosses over without being stopped and started again. Only once the scroll has stopped, 200 milliseconds after its last step, does the build-up drain away on its own, back to nothing within half a second of that last step, so a nudge into the stretch that goes no further never crosses over later. Momentum, and any scroll during a slide, add nothing to it.
77:The stretch is felt as well as seen. While anything has built up, the view at that end is pulled past its end, following the scroll but by less than it scrolled, and by less the further it is pulled, as a rubber band gives: at the start it moves nearly as far as the scroll, and by the barrier it has been pulled about 64 pixels, never more. Scrolling up at the latest task's top, its header and output move down together, leaving an empty band above them, in the body's colour; scrolling down at the previous tasks' bottom, they move up, leaving the band below them. The previous tasks row and the queue stay where they are, and nothing is drawn outside the space between them. The pull follows the build-up as it grows and drains, smoothly rather than in steps, so as the build-up drains the view springs back to its end, settling without bouncing. The view's own scroll position doesn't change while it is pulled; it is still at its end once it springs back.
78:While anything has built up against an end, a glow shows where the crossing will happen: a soft radial glow, centred in the space between the previous tasks row and the queue, fading from its middle to nothing at its edge, in the colour of the mode selected in the [ChatInputScope](../chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope), as the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope) colours it. It starts small and faint and grows larger and slightly brighter as the build-up nears the barrier, at its largest a little under the height of that space and still only a subtle wash of colour, never hiding what is beneath it. It follows the build-up as it grows and drains, smoothly rather than in steps. It never takes a click or a scroll. As the view crosses over, the glow fades out quickly while the slide begins; with nothing built up, there is no glow at all.
79:With the latest task's output scrolled to its top, a scroll up past the barrier expands the previous tasks, as clicking their row does, opening scrolled to the bottom, on the tasks sent most recently, as the [HistoryListScope](../../../ui/components/history-list/index.md#history-list-scope) says. Before any task has been sent, or with no previous tasks, scrolling up does nothing more: the view stops at its top without stretching, and no glow shows.
80:With the previous tasks expanded and scrolled to their bottom, a scroll down past the barrier closes them, as clicking "Back to the latest task" does, bringing back the latest task and its output as they were left.
81:However the previous tasks are closed, by a scroll or by clicking "Back to the latest task", the latest task's output comes back scrolled just where it was when they were opened, with its lock to the bottom as it was. Locked, it comes back at its bottom and still locked, showing whatever output arrived while the previous tasks were open, and goes on following new output. Unlocked, it comes back at the same place in its output, however much arrived meanwhile; if that place no longer exists, as when the latest task has changed since, it comes back at its top, unlocked.
82:A fling's momentum still running when an end is reached stops there, never pulling into the stretch or crossing over. Momentum is only what comes after the platform says the fingers have lifted from the trackpad; where it never says, as on Linux, no scroll is taken for momentum, and every one pulls into the stretch. Output or a list too short to scroll is always at both its ends, so any scroll over it that leads somewhere pulls into the stretch. Only the wheel or trackpad crosses over. Scrolling sideways, dragging a scrollbar to an end, and scrolling anything inside that scrolls on its own, such as an open task's table in the list, never do.
83:Crossing over by scrolling is animated, starting from wherever the stretch has pulled the view. Scrolling up, the previous tasks slide down into view from above, already scrolled to their bottom, pushing the latest task's header and output out below them, the two moving together as one column. Scrolling down, the latest task's header and output slide up into view from below, already scrolled where they will settle, pushing the previous tasks out above them. The slide is quick and settles without bouncing, as the right sidebar's does. Only the space between the previous tasks row and the queue moves, and nothing is drawn outside it; the row and the queue stay where they are, the row reading what it will once the slide settles, from the moment it starts.
84:The scroll that crosses over stops at the moment of the switch. The step that takes it past the barrier is used up by the crossing, all of it, however far past the barrier it reached, and none of it scrolls the view beneath. Whatever more of that same scroll follows, as the wheel keeps turning, the fingers keep moving, or a fling's momentum runs on, is swallowed: during the slide and after it has settled, it scrolls neither view, pulls into no stretch, and never crosses back, so the view it switched to is left exactly as it arrived, scrolled where the slide brought it. Only a new scroll moves anything again: one begun once the wheel or trackpad has been still for 80 milliseconds, counted from the last scroll step whether that came during the slide or after, or once fingers are lifted from the trackpad and put back. That new scroll behaves as any other, scrolling the view, or, with the view at its end, pulling into the stretch from its first step. Expanding or closing the previous tasks by clicking their row is not animated.
86:#### Changed Files
88:##### Description
90:In a project that is a git repository, every task, the latest and each of the previous tasks, lists the files that changed while it ran, between the two snapshots of the working tree taken as it started and ended, as the [ProjectDataScope](../../project-data/index.md#project-data-scope)'s task snapshots say. In a project that isn't one, no task shows any of this.
92:##### List
94:The files are those `git diff --name-status` gives between the two snapshots, each one added, modified, deleted, or renamed. Each is a row with its path in the project, a small letter for how it changed, A, M, D, or R, in the colour the git panel gives that change, and, for a renamed file, the path it was renamed from, muted, before an arrow. They are listed in path order, below the task's output, beneath the latest task's output table, and beneath an open previous task's table, headed "Files changed" with how many there are. The list is collapsed to its heading to start with, and expands when the heading is clicked.
95:Only the project's own files are listed, its spec, its code, and anything else of its own, never what the application keeps for
97:###### Itself
99:nothing in the project's .suspense directory, its history,
101:questions, reports, and the rest, as the [ProjectDataScope](../../project-data/index.md#project-data-scope) says, and not the draft, .suspense-draft.pi, wherever it is. They are left out of the list and of its count alike, for every task, those recorded before as well, and a file renamed into or out of .suspense is listed only by its path outside it, as added or deleted.
102:While a task is still running, it has only its first snapshot, so it shows no list yet. A task whose run changed nothing else, nothing at all or only what the application keeps, reads "No files changed", muted. A task with no snapshots, as one from before they were taken or one whose snapshot couldn't be taken, shows no list.
104:##### Who Changed
106:The snapshots catch everything that changed while the task ran, including the user's own edits made meanwhile, as in the side editor. Each file is compared with the files the harness's tool calls reported writing or editing, as the referenced spec works them out, from its file tools and its shell commands, a subagent's included. A file the agent reported is shown as changed by the agent, its row plain; any other is shown as changed during the task, its row muted, with a small clock icon and a tooltip saying it changed while the task ran but not through the agent.
108:##### Opening
110:Clicking a file opens its diff between the two snapshots, the file as it was when the task started against the file as it was when it ended, in the [DiffViewScope](../../../ui/components/diff-view/index.md#diff-view-scope), as the git panel opens a file's uncommitted changes.
112:#### Freeform
114:##### Description
116:A Freeform task is shown as a regular chat, not as a task: its prompt as a message on the right, and the harness's reply as a message on the left, read as prose, as the [AskConversationScope](../ask-conversation/index.md#ask-conversation-scope) shows a question and its answer.
118:##### Conversation
120:While the latest task was sent in Freeform, the space between the previous tasks row and the queue shows its conversation as a chat, in place of the latest task's header and output table. The chat holds the latest task and the Freeform tasks sent straight before it, back to the last task of another mode, or to the first that started a new conversation, oldest at the top and newest at the bottom. Sending another Freeform prompt adds it at the bottom; sending a task in any other mode shows that task as ever, and the chat goes with it.
122:##### Messages
124:Each prompt is shown as it was typed, in a box on the theme's raised surface, faintly tinted Freeform's grey, as the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope) colours it, with corners rounded 6 pixels, set against the chat's right edge and at most 80% of its width, with the text and images attached to it listed beneath its text. Beneath the box, at its right, a small muted line gives the time it was sent and, once its task is over, its Resend button, as the [PromptSendingScope](../sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) says; while it runs, its Cancel button is there instead. A message sent to the task while it ran is a box of its own, laid out the same way, placed among the reply where the harness took it in.
125:Each reply follows beneath its prompt, against the chat's left edge, at the chat's full width, with no box, laid out as the [AskConversationScope](../ask-conversation/index.md#ask-conversation-scope)'s answers are: the reply text after the harness's last tool call rendered as markdown in the body's text colour, everything before it summed up in one small muted line that expands into the steps, a status line with a spinner and the latest thing the harness did in that line's place while the task runs, and the error it failed with, "Cancelled", or "No answer." at its end. Beneath the reply, in a git repository, come the files changed while it ran, as every task lists them. Prompts are 16 pixels apart, and a reply starts 8 pixels beneath its prompt.
127:##### No Task Trappings
129:Nothing in the chat is shown as a task: there is no header, no status label, no hidden anchor's name, no compiled prompt, and no output table.

Scrolling sideways, dragging a scrollbar to an end, and scrolling anything inside that scrolls on its own, such as an open task's table in the list, never do.
83:Crossing over by scrolling is animated, starting from wherever the stretch has pulled the view. Scrolling up, the previous tasks slide down into view from above, already scrolled to their bottom, pushing the latest task's header and output out below them, the two moving together as one column. Scrolling down, the latest task's header and output slide up into view from below, already scrolled where they will settle, pushing the previous tasks out above them. The slide is quick and settles without bouncing, as the right sidebar's does. Only the space between the previous tasks row and the queue moves, and nothing is drawn outside it; the row and the queue stay where they are, the row reading what it will once the slide settles, from the moment it starts.
84:The scroll that crosses over stops at the moment of the switch. The step that takes it past the barrier is used up by the crossing, all of it, however far past the barrier it reached, and none of it scrolls the view beneath. Whatever more of that same scroll follows, as the wheel keeps turning, the fingers keep moving, or a fling's momentum runs on, is swallowed: during the slide and after it has settled, it scrolls neither view, pulls into no stretch, and never crosses back, so the view it switched to is left exactly as it arrived, scrolled where the slide brought it. Only a new scroll moves anything again: one begun once the wheel or trackpad has been still for 80 milliseconds, counted from the last scroll step whether that came during the slide or after, or once fingers are lifted from the trackpad and put back. That new scroll behaves as any other, scrolling the view, or, with the view at its end, pulling into the stretch from its first step. Expanding or closing the previous tasks by clicking their row is not animated.
86:#### Changed Files
88:##### Description
90:In a project that is a git repository, every task, the latest and each of the previous tasks, lists the files that changed while it ran, between the two snapshots of the working tree taken as it started and ended, as the [ProjectDataScope](../../project-data/index.md#project-data-scope)'s task snapshots say. In a project that isn't one, no task shows any of this.
92:##### List
94:The files are those `git diff --name-status` gives between the two snapshots, each one added, modified, deleted, or renamed. Each is a row with its path in the project, a small letter for how it changed, A, M, D, or R, in the colour the git panel gives that change, and, for a renamed file, the path it was renamed from, muted, before an arrow. They are listed in path order, below the task's output, beneath the latest task's output table, and beneath an open previous task's table, headed "Files changed" with how many there are. The list is collapsed to its heading to start with, and expands when the heading is clicked.
95:Only the project's own files are listed, its spec, its code, and anything else of its own, never what the application keeps for
97:###### Itself
99:nothing in the project's .suspense directory, its history,
101:questions, reports, and the rest, as the [ProjectDataScope](../../project-data/index.md#project-data-scope) says, and not the draft, .suspense-draft.pi, wherever it is. They are left out of the list and of its count alike, for every task, those recorded before as well, and a file renamed into or out of .suspense is listed only by its path outside it, as added or deleted.
102:While a task is still running, it has only its first snapshot, so it shows no list yet. A task whose run changed nothing else, nothing at all or only what the application keeps, reads "No files changed", muted. A task with no snapshots, as one from before they were taken or one whose snapshot couldn't be taken, shows no list.

106:The snapshots catch everything that changed while the task ran, including the user's own edits made meanwhile, as in the side editor. 110:Clicking a file opens its diff between the two snapshots, the file as it was when the task started against the file as it was when it ended, in the [DiffViewScope](../../../ui/components/diff-view/index.md#diff-view-scope), as the git panel opens a file's uncommitted changes.
112:#### Freeform
114:##### Description
116:A Freeform task is shown as a regular chat, not as a task: its prompt as a message on the right, and the harness's reply as a message on the left, read as prose, as the [AskConversationScope](../ask-conversation/index.md#ask-conversation-scope) shows a question and its answer.
118:##### Conversation
120:While the latest task was sent in Freeform, the space between the previous tasks row and the queue shows its conversation as a chat, in place of the latest task's header and output table. 124:Each prompt is shown as it was typed, in a box on the theme's raised surface, faintly tinted Freeform's grey, as the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope) colours it, with corners rounded 6 pixels, set against the chat's right edge and at most 80% of its width, with the text and images attached to it listed beneath its text. 125:Each reply follows beneath its prompt, against the chat's left edge, at the chat's full width, with no box, laid out as the [AskConversationScope](../ask-conversation/index.md#ask-conversation-scope)'s answers are: the reply text after the harness's last tool call rendered as markdown in the body's text colour, everything before it summed up in one small muted line that expands into the steps, a status line with a spinner and the latest thing the harness did in that line's place while the task runs, and the error it failed with, "Cancelled", or "No answer." at its end. 127:##### No Task Trappings
129:Nothing in the chat is shown as a task: there is no header, no status label, no hidden anchor's name, no compiled prompt, and no output table.

# Prompt Editor

## How To Build

A PromptEditor should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A PromptEditor should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, intergration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../ui/theme/index.md#theme-scope): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Concept

### Pitch

An interface for sending tasks to a local coding harness like Claude Code, written directly with compiled-on-depand Piton.

### Shape

#### Description

Not a chat. Each prompt sent is a task for the harness, tasks can queue, and each task shows its output until it finishes. There are no message bubbles.

#### Basic Design And Layout

The [MessageList](./message-list/index.md#message-list) fills the body's Chat tab: all the space between the body's tab bar and the [ChatInputScope](./chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) along the bottom. From top to bottom it holds the previous tasks row, the header for the latest task, the latest task's output, and the queue.
Before any task has been sent, the space shows a hint instead, which wraps when the view is narrow. It reads "Write a prompt below. Enter adds a line; Ctrl/Cmd+Enter sends it." or, while no project is open, as the [NoProjectStateScope](../no-project/index.md#no-project-state-scope) says, "Open a project to start prompting."

#### Chat History

[MessageList](./message-list/index.md#message-list)

#### Previous Tasks

Previous tasks are a [HistoryListScope](../../ui/components/history-list/index.md#history-list-scope) along the top of the view, listing every task sent. Its row counts every task but the latest, which heads the view: "No previous tasks", "1 previous task", or "N previous tasks", and each offers Resend. Expanded, the list takes the place of the latest task and its output, and the row reads "Back to the latest task".
Every task in the list has a checkbox at the left of its heading, before its status, and clicking it selects or deselects the task without opening or closing it. Shift-clicking one selects every task between it and the one last clicked, never deselecting any; with none clicked before, it selects or deselects that one as a plain click does. The selection is kept while the list is closed and opened again, until it is cleared or sent. Each open project keeps its own, as the [OpenProjectsScope](../open-projects/index.md#open-projects-scope) says.
While any task is selected, the row shows the batch actions at its right, in place of nothing: "N selected", muted, counting every task selected, then "Send N to Spec" and "Send N to Code", small ghost buttons with a swap icon, each tinted the colour of the mode it sends to, then "Clear", which deselects them all. I changed the spec so the header shows every task under way, with one selected in full and the rest as compact rows. `piton check` reports no problems, `piton build` wrote 79 files, and the new "Running Tasks" section is in the refreshed reference.

## What changed in the spec

**1. New "Running Tasks" section** (`.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/message-list/index.md#running-tasks`, from the new `spec/scope/prompt-mode/message-list/RunningTasks.pi`)
- **What the header holds:** the latest task plus every other task that is building, compiling or running, such as a Spec task and a Code task running at once.
- **Selected task:** only one is selected. It shows in full: compiled prompt, hidden anchor's name, status and elapsed time, buttons, and beneath it its output table and changed files.
- **Compact rows (`#compact-row`):** the others are one-line rows stacked above the selected task, oldest at the top.
  - Each is 28px tall, faintly tinted in its mode's colour, with a thin line between rows.
  - Each shows its status label and elapsed time, the first line of its prompt (cut off with an ellipsis), and its Cancel button while it's under way. Nothing else.
  - The tooltip gives the prompt's first lines and its mode.
- **Only one task:** with nothing else under way there are no compact rows, and the header looks as it does today.
- **Selecting (`#selecting`):**
  - Clicking a compact row selects it straight away, with no animation, and the previously selected task becomes a compact row.
  - Each task keeps its scroll position and bottom lock while another is selected.
  - The right sidebar follows the selected task while it runs.
  - A newly sent task is selected once it starts building. Otherwise the selection only moves when you click.
  - A task that isn't the latest leaves the header once it has finished and isn't selected. If it finishes while selected, it stays until you pick another.
  - The latest task always stays.
  - Each open project keeps its own selection.
- **Previous tasks (`#previous-tasks`):** tasks shown in the header aren't in the previous tasks list and aren't counted in its row.

**2. Supporting changes**
- **Layout** (`.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/index.md`, `#basic-design-and-layout` and `#previous-tasks`): the view's layout and the previous tasks row count are updated to match.
- **Cancelling** (`.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/sending/index.md#cancelling`): Cancel sits on the selected task's header. Each compact row has its own Cancel, and clicking it never selects the row. A task running in the other lane no longer shows among the previous tasks as "Running".
- **Activity list** (`.claude/reference/scope/running-activity/index.md#list`): clicking a running task there selects it in the header and shows its output in full, rather than opening it among the previous tasks.

The constraints are in `.suspense/history/1791132300-Prompt_ea29fc7e259b1dbd.understanding.md`.

## Anchors the code should follow
